chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Rib'i from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The testimony of women is not valid in cases of blood money (qisas/diyyah).
The explanation/ruling regarding it is also what we have previously mentioned in other narrations.
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of women's testimony in Islamic inheritance or blood money cases according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the general principle that women's testimony is invalid in *qatl* (blood money or retribution) cases, a ruling often debated in Shia jurisprudence regarding whether it applies to all types of homicide or specific contexts. The narrator’s closing remark directs readers to cross-reference other hadiths in the collection, highlighting the methodological reliance on reconciling apparent contradictions across the four major Shia hadith collections. This reflects the broader scholarly discourse on whether the exclusion is due to a lack of precision in women's testimony or a specific legal dispensation (*rukhsa*).
